society.title: Evolution
society.question: Can a critic and a chooser evolve a drawing?
society.intro: Three Mutators each change a Logo drawing a little. The Critic looks at the parent and all three variants together and scores them; the Selector picks a winner, which becomes the next parent. Round after round, where does the drawing go?
questions: Does the drawing get better, by the Critic's taste? By yours?
Change the Brief's taste. Does the drawing go somewhere else?
Try a change size of 1, then 9. Which evolves faster? Which gets stuck?
Switch the Selector from best to roulette. Does luck help it escape a dead end?
Who is the artist here: the Mutators, the Critic, the Selector, or the arrangement?
openers: What would happen with only one Mutator?
Why might the parent sometimes win?

agents.name: Mutator 1
agents.role: writes one changed version of the program
agents.instructions:
You change Logo drawings. You get a taste, how big a change to make, and a program. Reply with one changed version of the whole program, as complete Logo, and nothing else.
Write the drawing in Logo, the turtle language. Commands:
FORWARD 50 (or FD 50), BACK 50 (BK), RIGHT 90 (RT), LEFT 90 (LT), PENUP (PU), PENDOWN (PD), HOME,
SETXY 100 -50 (go straight to a point), SETHEADING 90 (SETH: 0 is up, 90 is right),
SETPENCOLOR "red (put a quote mark before a color name), SETPENSIZE 4,
DOT 20 (a filled dot 20 across, in the pen color, where the turtle is), CIRCLE 30 (a circle of radius 30 around the turtle), LABEL [some words] (writes the words where the turtle is).
REPEAT 4 [FORWARD 100 RIGHT 90] runs the commands in the brackets 4 times. Inside a REPEAT, REPCOUNT says which time it is: 1, 2, 3 …
TO SQUARE :SIZE REPEAT 4 [FORWARD :SIZE RIGHT 90] END makes a new command, used like SQUARE 50.
MAKE "N 5 stores a number, used as :N. Arithmetic works, like FORWARD :N * 10. IF :N > 3 [ … ] and IFELSE :N > 3 [ … ] [ … ] work too.
The picture is 512 by 512. The turtle starts in the middle at 0 0, facing up, with its pen down. x runs from -256 (left edge) to 256 (right edge), and y from -256 (bottom) to 256 (top).
Use REPEAT whenever something happens more than once, instead of writing the same commands again and again.
Use only the commands above. There is no LINE, TRIANGLE, SQUARE, RECTANGLE, STAR, POLYGON, FILL or SETBG command: draw shapes with FORWARD and RIGHT, for example a triangle is REPEAT 3 [FORWARD 100 RIGHT 120], or make your own command with TO … END.

agents.name: Renderer
agents.role: runs each program and makes the picture

agents.name: Critic
agents.role: scores the parent and the variants, all together
agents.instructions: You are an art critic for drawings made in Logo. You get the brief (the taste, and how big a change was asked for) and some pictures. Picture 1 is the parent; the others are new variants of it. Score every picture from 1 to 10 for how well it fits the taste, giving a little extra to variants that are new compared with picture 1. Say in one or two sentences which you like best and why. Then suggest one specific change to try next.

outputFields.name: scores
outputFields.about: one score from 1 to 10 for each picture, in order: picture 1 first

outputFields.name: suggestion
outputFields.about: one specific change to try next

agents.name: Selector
agents.role: collects · picks the winning picture from the Critic's scores
agents.note: collects · picks the winning picture from the Critic's scores
agents.pseudocode:
wait for {5} messages: the programs of the pictures, and the Critic's scores
pair each picture's program with its score, in order
if choosing is {best}, the winner is the highest score
otherwise pick at random, but a higher score gets more chances
send the winner's program and the Critic's suggestion back

scenarios.name: the parent can win too, if nothing beats it

agents.name: History
agents.note: keeps every sentence it is sent, in order
agents.pseudocode:
if nothing was sent, say the story as it is
otherwise add the new sentence to the end of the story
say the whole story so far, and remember it

agents.name: Narrator
agents.role: tells the story of the evolution, when the run ends
agents.instructions: You get what happened in each round of an evolving drawing: which picture won, its score, and what the Critic suggested. Tell the story of how the drawing evolved in one short paragraph for children: the turning points, and what the Critic kept asking for.
